oewn-07155056-n.learner: words that show you are pleased about someone else's success or good luck (the word is usually plural).
examples: Elizabeth's congratulations were given with a sincerity, a warmth, a delight, which words could but poorly express.
He addressed himself directly to Miss Bennet with a polite congratulation

oewn-06646403-n.learner: the act of telling someone that you know they have a reason to celebrate.
examples: Bingley replied that he did, and made his congratulations.
"I must trouble you once more for congratulations.

oewn-07289130-n.learner: the act of bending your head, body, or knee to show respect, to show you give in, to show shame, or to greet someone.
examples: Her cousin prefaced his speech with a solemn bow
And with a bow to Mr. Darcy, he concluded his speech

oewn-02882960-n.learner: a weapon for shooting arrows, made of a curved piece of springy wood with a tight cord that drives the arrow forward.
examples: He drew the bow and sent an arrow into the target.

oewn-02883431-n.learner: a knot with two loops and two loose ends, the kind used to tie shoelaces.
examples: She tied her shoelaces in a neat bow.

oewn-07591075-n.learner: a small meal in the middle of the afternoon, with tea and sandwiches or cakes.
examples: When the gentlemen had joined them, and tea was over, the card tables were placed.
It was not till the afternoon, when he joined them at tea

oewn-07949514-n.learner: a drink made by letting tea leaves sit in water.
examples: They were interrupted by Miss Bennet, who came to fetch her mother's tea.

oewn-07949081-n.learner: the dried leaves of the tea bush, used for making the drink.
examples: She spooned some tea into the warmed pot.
hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet's civilities

oewn-00460251-v.learner: to push someone or something to go faster than is natural.
examples: hurried her away to her room
The driver hurried the tired horses along the rough road.

oewn-00460453-v.learner: to do what you are doing at high speed.
examples: Hurry, or we shall miss the coach.

oewn-07531593-n.learner: a strong feeling that is aimed at some wrong done to you, whether the wrong is real or only imagined.
examples: my anger soon began to take a proper direction
All Elizabeth's anger against him had been long done away
His complexion became pale with anger

oewn-00760325-n.learner: a readiness to fight stirred up by a wrong, real or imagined, pictured as one of the deadly sins.
examples: Anger is counted among the seven deadly sins.

connotation.why: casts the feeling as one of the deadly sins

oewn-01075919-n.learner: the act of getting in the way of something so that it is blocked or slowed down.
examples: She looked at her father to entreat his interference, lest Mary should be singing all night.
never had she before been so much disposed to pardon his interference in the views of his friend

connotation.why: casts a person's stepping in as unwanted meddling

oewn-06674307-n.learner: a policy of stepping into the affairs of other countries.
examples: The treaty was meant to end all interference in the affairs of neighbouring states.

oewn-03525974-n.learner: anything in the way that blocks you or weighs you down.
examples: The low branches were an interference to anyone walking the path.
She had not at first thought very seriously of going thither
Elizabeth again, and more seriously, assured her of its truth.

oewn-00016415-r.learner: to a severe or grave degree.
examples: I am most seriously displeased.
He was seriously hurt in the fall.

oewn-06295743-n.learner: a run of words put together in a way the grammar of a language allows.
examples: What think you of this sentence, my dear Lizzy?"
Elizabeth tried to unite civility and truth in a few short sentences

oewn-01191772-n.learner: in criminal law, a court's final decision that a person is guilty, together with the punishment given.
examples: The judge passed sentence on the prisoner that same morning.

oewn-15249488-n.learner: the length of time a prisoner is kept in prison.
examples: He served a sentence of five years.

oewn-05759704-n.learner: fine taste in what is proper, and care not to hurt or embarrass other people.
examples: however your natural delicacy may lead you to dissemble
I think it would not be very likely to promote sisterly affection or delicacy of mind.

oewn-04849260-n.learner: quiet skill in handling a situation.
examples: it is happy for you that you possess the talent of flattering with delicacy

oewn-04820315-n.learner: the quality of being beautiful and finely made to look at.
examples: The delicacy of the lace made it look like frost on a window.

oewn-02243552-v.learner: to get something by making a special effort.
examples: My object has been to secure an amiable companion for myself
I wonder he does not marry, to secure a lasting convenience of that kind.
These rules secure the safety of everyone on board.

oewn-01343121-v.learner: to make something hold firmly in place.
examples: She secured the shutters with a heavy bolt.
